increments.title: The test plan names the break for every criterion
increments.goal: The researcher's test-plan contract requires, for every acceptance criterion of an increment, at least one case that fails when that criterion's behaviour is broken or removed, with the breaking production change stated as part of each case and a stated reason in the plan wherever a criterion is left without such a case; the mutation standard behind this is stated on exactly one owning page, and every other page that needs it points at that owner instead of restating it.
criteria: The researcher's page requires the test plan to name, for every acceptance criterion of the increment, at least one case that fails when that criterion's behaviour is broken or removed.

steps.label: research:name-the-break.0

return.plan:
Give the mutation standard one owner and wire the two role pages to it. Ownership decision: the standard lands in the shared brief, skills/agent-brief/SKILL.md — it is the only page preloaded into every agent, so both the researcher (who plans to the standard) and the reviewer (who judges by it) hold the owner's text at runtime. Rejected: ownership on agents/reviewer.md (today's only live statement) or on agents/researcher.md — either one leaves the other role with a pointer it cannot dereference at runtime, since no role page is in another role's context; the originating issue docs/issues/2026-08-07-agile-loop-optimizations already named the agent-brief as the place 'where every role can read it'. Rejected: touching workflows/agile-loop.js — I read its prompt builders; they carry field names and criteria, never the standard, so no workflow change is needed. Rejected: any file-path cross-reference between pages — point by name ('the shared brief'), because test-repo.sh's handoff guard (line 327) flags any agent-page filename not preceded by a slash.

Three edits, exact text (the test-author pins these phrases by grep, so use them verbatim):

1. skills/agent-brief/SKILL.md — insert a new section between '## The commands that count' and '## Your step return':

## The mutation standard

A criterion counts as tested only when at least one of its tests fails if the
behaviour it asks for is broken or removed — and a test earns its place by its
break: the production change it exists to catch. This page owns that standard;
a page that needs it points here instead of restating it. What your role does
with it — plan to it, write to it, judge by it — is your own page's to say.

Leave the closing '## What this is not' section untouched: the new section delegates application to the role pages, so 'this page is not your role' stays true.

2. agents/researcher.md — in '## The test plan', replace the whole '**What.**' bullet with:

- **What.** Per acceptance criterion, the cases that prove it: input, state,
  expected result, and the edges — empty, limit, repeat. Hold the plan to the
  shared brief's mutation standard: every acceptance criterion gets at least
  one case that fails when that criterion's behaviour is broken or removed,
  and each case states, as part of the case, the break — the production
  change that would make it fail. Where you leave a criterion without such a
  case, the plan itself says so and why, and the same goes for anything else
  you leave untested: the omission reads as a decision. A criterion missing
  from this list gets no test at all.

This replaces (not supplements) the old 'Name what you leave untested and why' sentence — the brief forbids stating one rule twice. Touch nothing else on the page; the 'How.' bullet's 'suite doc' wording is pinned by test-repo.sh line 1610.

3. agents/reviewer.md — in check 3 ('The tests against the intent'), replace the sentence 'Would each criterion have a test that fails if the behaviour breaks, and are its edges covered?' with: 'Hold them, criterion by criterion, to the mutation standard the shared brief owns, edges included.' Everything else in check 3 and the page stays — the probe sections and the backlog.json wording are pinned by existing suite cases.

Hard constraints on all new prose (existing test-repo.sh guards ban these tokens in agent pages and shipped skills): no 'rulebook' (line 185), no 'argus'/'collector'/'OTEL_'/'UROBOROS_OBS' (line 244), no 'probe' outside reviewer.md (line 1576), no 'chain depth' outside planner.md (line 455), no 'handoff' in any spelling (line 343), no 'Apache' (line 48), no agent-page filename without a leading slash (line 327), and never create a CLAUDE.md at the repository root (line 176 fails the suite if one exists). The defining phrase 'counts as tested' must appear in SKILL.md and in no other agent page or shipped skill — it is the single-owner grep anchor.

The test-author (not the implementer) adds the new grep cases to test-repo.sh; the implementer edits only the three markdown pages.

agents/researcher.md — researcher role page; edit point is the '**What.**' bullet of '## The test plan'.
agents/reviewer.md — reviewer role page; edit point is one sentence in check 3 '**The tests against the intent.**'.
test-repo.sh — the repository-facts suite (bash ok/no grep cases, ~1648 lines, includes an embedded node driver for the workflow); the new pin cases land here, test-author's file.
Codemap verdict: accurate and complete for this increment. Both of its 'touched only if' candidates resolve to touched — ownership lands in SKILL.md, and the requirement is pinned in test-repo.sh. workflows/agile-loop.js needs no change (its prompts never state the standard).

There is no linter and no formatter for markdown or shell in this repository. The full ./test.sh is not part of this change's commands.
return.testPlan:
Whether: tests, yes. The change is prose, but this repository's own suite pins page content by grep, and every criterion here is grep-checkable — that is the established convention (see the probe and chain-depth single-owner cases).

Suite doc: test-repo.sh has no CLAUDE.md suite doc, and must not get one — the suite itself fails if a CLAUDE.md exists at the repository root (case near line 176: it would load as inheritable project memory). Do not create one; this is the stated exception the researcher contract asks me to name. The conventions, read from the file itself: ok "..."/no "..." helpers increment pass/fail counters; each case carries a comment naming the drift it exists to catch; thematic sections open with a blank echo plus echo "=== title"; paths go through "$root"; command substitutions that may match nothing end in || true (the file runs under set -u); single-owner cases follow the chain_depth_owners / reviewer_probe_owners pattern — grep -lie '<phrase>' "$root"/agents/*.md "$root"/skills/*/SKILL.md compared against the owner's path, mismatch echoed indented.

All cases: level repository-suite, file test-repo.sh at the repo root, framework bash ok/no cases, command `bash test-repo.sh` (the suite has no per-case runner; it is cheap enough to run whole). Suggested placement: one new section, e.g. echo "=== the mutation standard has one owner", after the '=== the planner alone owns the chain depth it decides' section it mirrors — exact placement is the test-author's call.

Criterion 1 — the researcher's page requires a per-criterion go-red case:
- Case 1: agents/researcher.md matches both 'at least one case' and 'broken or removed' (grep -qi, two greps ANDed). Break that makes it fail: delete from the '**What.**' bullet the sentence 'Hold the plan to the shared brief's mutation standard: every acceptance criterion gets at least one case that fails when that criterion's behaviour is broken or removed'.

Criterion 2 — each planned case states the break:
- Case 2: agents/researcher.md matches 'production change' (grep -qi). Break: remove the clause 'the break — the production change that would make it fail' from that bullet.

Criterion 3 — one owning page, others point:
- Case 3: skills/agent-brief/SKILL.md contains the heading '## The mutation standard' (grep -q). Break: delete the brief's section.
- Case 4 (single owner): grep -lie 'counts as tested' over "$root"/agents/*.md and "$root"/skills/*/SKILL.md equals exactly "$root/skills/agent-brief/SKILL.md". Break, both directions: restate the defining sentence on any agent page or second skill (two paths match), or delete it from the brief (none match).
- Case 5 (the pointers): agents/researcher.md matches 'mutation standard' and agents/reviewer.md matches 'mutation standard' (grep -qi each). Break: drop either page's pointer — e.g. revert reviewer check 3 to its pre-change wording.
- Case 6 (the old restatement is gone): agents/reviewer.md does NOT match 'fails if the behaviour breaks' (grep -qi, inverted). Break: reinstate the old free-standing question in check 3.

Criterion 4 — a gap says so and why in the plan itself:
- Case 7: agents/researcher.md matches 'says so and why' (grep -Eqi 'says? so and why'). Break: delete 'Where you leave a criterion without such a case, the plan itself says so and why' from the bullet.

Untested, as decisions: (a) a paraphrased restatement of the standard on another page evades any grep — case 4 pins the canonical phrase, and the review's reading covers paraphrase; exact-word pinning is this suite's accepted convention. (b) Whether future researchers actually deliver break-naming plans is runtime behaviour of other repositories' runs; no case here can check it — the pages are the deliverable. (c) No absence-pin for workflows/agile-loop.js: I read its prompt builders and they never state the standard, and this suite pins absences only where drift has happened once.

Already red: I ran nothing in this step — no baseline run, per contract, and no plan question needed one. From reading: all seven new cases go red against today's pages until the implementer's edits land (that is the intended order — tests first), and no existing case is affected, because the planned page text avoids every token the existing guards ban (rulebook, argus/collector/OTEL_/UROBOROS_OBS, probe outside reviewer.md, chain depth, any spelling of hand-off, Apache, agent-page filenames without a leading slash) and no root CLAUDE.md is created.

What counts as done, the closed list: `bash test-repo.sh` — exit 0. Nothing else; ./test.sh's other suites (worktree, recorder, hooks, tools) cover files this change never touches.
return.summary: The mutation standard gets one owner — a short section in the shared brief, the only page every role holds at runtime — and the researcher's test-plan contract now demands a go-red case per criterion with its break named, the reviewer's check pointing at the owner instead of restating it; seven grep cases in the repository suite pin all four criteria.
